Evidence_Text: Comprehensive review of multiple sclerosis should consider mobility, balance, upper-limb function and other neurological or functional difficulties relevant to the individual patient.
Multiple sclerosis may affect multiple neurological and functional domains, and clinical assessment should consider patient history, physical examination and neurological symptoms.
The nature and extent of disability should be documented as part of the comprehensive review of a person with multiple sclerosis.
Issues identified during comprehensive multiple sclerosis review should be considered within specialist or multidisciplinary clinical care and referred to appropriate professionals when necessary.
Multiple sclerosis assessment should consider sensory symptoms, pain and visual problems because these may contribute to the patient's functional difficulties.
Assessment of multiple sclerosis should consider multiple sources of clinical information rather than interpreting an individual symptom or measurement in isolation.
Adults with multiple sclerosis should receive a comprehensive review at least annually by healthcare professionals with expertise in multiple sclerosis.
